metadata.description: A point-in-time copy of one Volume's data, that a new Volume can be restored from. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): Kubernetes VolumeSnapshot, CSI CreateSnapshot and the snapshot of every block and file provisioner (ZFS, Ceph RBD, LVM, cloud disks) abstract to the same thing, so an order for a snapshot of a volume is fillable by whatever provisions the volume. The provisioner is the provider.

deletion_policy.description: What happens to the snapshot's data when the record is released: Delete or Retain.

snapshot_handle.description: The provider's snapshot id once Realized (CSI snapshot_id, a ZFS `dataset@snapshot` name). Read by the provider to restore or delete it.

restore_size.description: A quantity (common-elements), the smallest capacity a Volume restored from this snapshot needs (Kubernetes status.restoreSize). Read when a restore is ordered, to refuse a target smaller than the data.

relationships.name: snapshot_of
relationships.description: The volume this snapshot copies (spec.source names it).

adopts.role: point-in-time copy vocabulary (source, deletionPolicy, restoreSize, snapshotHandle), names mirrored in snake_case

context.purpose: Declares a point-in-time copy of a volume's data that a new volume can be restored from.
context.plain_description: A snapshot of one volume, taken at one moment. It names the volume it copies (`source`) and what happens to its data when the record is released (`deletion_policy`). Once realized, the provider reports its handle and how large a volume restored from it must be. Whether it is ready to restore from is a `Ready` status condition, not a field. A new Volume restores from it by naming it in `data_source`.
use_when: You need a point-in-time copy of a volume to restore, clone or move its data from.
You need a restored volume's lineage, which snapshot of which volume it came from, kept in the graph.
not_for: Continuous replication of a volume to another site, which is a different relationship (a stream, not a copy).
A backup held outside the provisioner, which is not restorable by the provisioner alone.
works_with: Volume — the volume it copies (`source`), and the volumes restored from it (their `data_source`).
